### Paper 1: Beyond EDA — A Systematic Review of Multimodal Sympathetic Nervous System Arousal Classification for Stress Detection

Sosa et al. (2026) conducted a systematic review comparing unimodal EDA-based stress detection against multimodal approaches that combine EDA with complementary signals such as heart rate variability (HRV), photoplethysmography (PPG), skin temperature (SKT), and SpO2. The review highlights that while EDA directly measures sympathetic nervous system arousal, HRV reflects primarily parasympathetic activity, meaning neither signal alone captures the full autonomic picture. Multimodal models consistently outperformed single-sensor approaches, particularly in real-world settings where physical activity and environmental noise impair single-sensor reliability. This paper is directly relevant to our project as it justifies combining EDA, respiration, and temperature signals rather than relying on heart rate alone, which is the approach taken in the team's previous papers.

### Paper 2: EDA, PPG and Skin Temperature as Predictive Signals for Mental Failure by a Statistical Analysis on Stress and Mental Workload

Luzzani et al. (2024) studied the statistical relationship between EDA, PPG, and skin temperature signals and stress or mental workload levels using Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests on 43 extracted features from cognitive stress tasks. Around 50% of features showed statistical evidence of differentiating relaxed from altered emotional conditions, and 15 features were found sufficient to simultaneously detect both stress and mental workload. The skin conductance level (SCL) mean was highlighted as clearly separating the relaxed class from stressed states. This paper is directly relevant to our project as it provides the statistical framework for converting continuous physiological variables into categorical stress states, supporting the threshold-based rules our team is building for EDA, respiration, and temperature signals.
